summary: Interleaved embedding batch ordering anomaly causing rerank instability and sporadic latency spikes
description: Issue summary: Several rerank requests from a single customer intermittently return inconsistent top-k ordering despite identical inputs. Some requests also experience short latency spikes (~200-600ms extra) concurrently. Impact: Customer-visible rerank quality regressions and unpredictable latency for a subset of queries during peak traffic in eu-west. Environment: Dedicated pool for AcuteSearch Labs in eu-west, serving openlm-7b-emb-384 for embeddings and redwood-rerank-v2 for rerank scoring. Occurs intermittently, ~0.5-2% of requests during peak. Expected behaviour: Deterministic embedding vectors per input and stable rerank ordering for identical input sets. Actual behaviour: Identical queries (same prompt and doc set) sometimes yield different rankings; embeddings differ in a small subset of dimensions and cosine similarity changes enough to alter top-k. Temporary workaround: Customer pinned rerank pipeline to single-threaded encoder and disabled autoprefetch; reduces frequency but not fully eliminated.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer's test harness and payload (they provided examples) in prod eu-west. 2) Send batch of 24 queries with identical reference document set using embeddings endpoint + rerank flow. 3) Repeat the same batch 10 times. 4) Observe that 1-2 of the runs return a different top-5 ordering; inspect embedding vectors returned for differences. 5) Correlate with autoscaling logs and request trace IDs to identify timing overlap with new workers being provisioned.

investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: shape/dimension mismatch after fallback to quantized kernels. Reproduced locally only when kernel selection differs within tightly interleaved batches.
- Checked scheduler logs: autoscaler launched an additional worker at 14:22:02Z and new worker joined serving pool at 14:22:03Z, causing two concurrent batch flushes.
- Found a race in batch buffer metadata: when two batches flush to the same GPU worker during transition, the per-request offset metadata could be overwritten for a small subset of interleaved items. This led to swapped slice assignment in the final output tensor for affected requests.
- Confirmed with instrumented run: enabling strict mutex on batch commit eliminates the misalignment, and deterministic rerank outputs return.
- Observed latency spikes correlate with worker join events and increased kernel negotiation time (fp16 -> quantized path).
- Related to scheduling change introduced in PR 1842 (see linked PR).
comments: Support (Maya): Customer reports nondeterministic rerank order for identical inputs, intermittent latency. Provided sample traces and a small harness. Asked for priority review.
Customer (AcuteSearch Labs, eng@acutesearch.com): We observe 1-2% of requests flip top-5. Example trace IDs uploaded. This impacts relevance tuning — please advise ASAP.
SRE (Noah Chen): Correlated incident windows with autoscaler events in eu-west. Flagged possible race during worker onboarding. Collecting more traces.

Infra Eng (Liam): Instrumented batch commit path and reproduced locally. Found metadata overwrite race when two flushes target same worker concurrently. Drafting quick fix to serialize commit and add a unit test.
Support (Maya): Notified customer of in-progress fix and suggested temporary mitigation (pin single kernel + reduce concurrency). Customer will test and report back.
root_cause: A race condition in the serving-runtime batch commit logic allowed per-request offset metadata to be overwritten when interleaved batch flushes targeted the same GPU worker during autoscaler transitions. Kernel heterogeneity (fp16 vs quantized) increased race surface and timing variance, exposing the bug.
resolution: Applied a patch to the serving-runtime to atomically commit batch metadata and to validate per-request offsets before tensor assembly (hotfix deployed to eu-west dedicated pool 2026-03-14 07:18Z). Added a safety check that rejects and retries a batch flush if metadata checksum mismatch detected. Rollout: hotfix staged to canary hosts then to all dedicated eu-west workers. Observed no regressions in canary and customer confirmed decreased occurrence to 0% in follow-up tests.
follow_up_tasks: Backfill unit/integration tests that simulate interleaved flushes across mixed kernel selections (assigned to infra-team).
Add metric and alert: batch_metadata_checksum_failures (SLO: 0) and correlate with autoscaler events.
Postmortem doc to be created and linked to this ticket; include remediation and timeline (owner: Maya).
Consider redesign: stronger contract between scheduler and worker during join to avoid concurrent targeting of newly joining worker until it warms up.
